messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 page — KMS API errors and high latency detected. Multiple hosts failing startup due to KMS decrypt/sign timeouts in prod (primarily us-east-1). Auto-escalating to on-call. See runbook: https://go/runbooks/kms-dependency

sre-jordan: I'm on it. Marking as P1. Which services are failing to start? Any customer-facing outages yet?

eng-ryan: hitting this in ingress/ingester clusters. Example log from a failed pod:
```
ERROR 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z startup.go:142 KMS: failed to decrypt envelope key: context deadline exceeded
stack: kms_client.go:87 -> signer.go:45 -> startup.go:140
```
We also see signing requests timing out causing request re-sign loops.

support-anya: Noticed elevated incident reports from a handful of enterprise customers — 5 customers reporting elevated 5xx for API calls which correlate to service start/reload windows. No broad user-facing outage yet but increased error rates.

maria-ops: Preliminary checklist: 1) throttle new deploys to avoid storming KMS, 2) flip non-critical services to local software signer fallback, 3) increase KMS client timeouts & apply jittered backoff. Which of these can we do immediately?

eng-ryan: Can do (1) and (2) quickly. For (2) we have a feature-flag controlled fallback: set `ENABLE_SOFTWARE_SIGNER=true` in config-store for ingester/ingress. Patch command (k8s configmap update):
```bash
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/ingester ENABLE_SOFTWARE_SIGNER=true --overwrite
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/ingester
```
This will allow pods to start without hitting KMS for every envelope, we still use cached envelope keys for persisted secrets.

maria-ops: I'll apply the flag to ingester canary first and watch. On it.

deploy-bot: start_deploy: deployment/ingester -> canary -> user=deploy-bot -> job=deploy-789

eng-sam: FYI the software signer is less preferred for PCI workloads. We should ring-fence customers that require hardware-backed keys. I suggest we only enable fallback for non-PCI tenants. We'll adjust the rollout constraints in the config.

sre-jordan: Agreed. maria, don't enable for dedicated/enterprise tenants flagged as HSM-required. Only apply to default pool.

maria-ops: Applied to canary. Observability: KMS latency graphs show 99th percentile spiking from ~300ms to 8s starting at 10:05 UTC in us-east-1. Retry rates also spiked. Link: https://observability/r/abcd

eng-ryan: After canary flip, two canary pods started successfully with software signer. Request rate to KMS from our fleet dropped ~30%. Error rates on ingester decreased from 6% to 0.5% (canary) within 2 minutes. Rolling to rest of pool now but paused for handoff.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: @sre-jordan handing off to @eng-ryan in 10 minutes for ongoing mitigation and provider coordination.

support-anya: Customer impact summary for on-call handoff: ~1200 requests/min with transient 5xx across multiple customers; 5 customers reporting repeated failures. No data loss reported. Customers using Dedicated instances are mostly unaffected due to local KMS cache, but a few dedicated customers reported startup issues during internal restarts.

eng-ryan: I'm starting provider escalation with cloud KMS support — opening ticket with trace samples and request ids. Pattern: HEAD /sign requests timing out, errors `504 Gateway Timeout` from KMS endpoint. Ticket: https://cloud.kms/support/tickets/INC-1623 (placeholder).

maria-ops: Also enabling more aggressive local envelope caching for 15m TTL to reduce KMS dependency while provider recovers. Command: update configmap `kms-config` TTL -> 900s. Applying now.

eng-sam: Patching the signer client to add exponential backoff and increase socket timeout from 2s -> 10s as an emergency measure. Will push as a hotfix to runtime agents (non-disruptive config change where possible).

deploy-bot: patch_job: signer-hotfix -> rollout started -> jobs=3

incident-bot: Added incident timeline entry. Severity: P1. Incident lead: sre-jordan. Pager duty: pagers notified.

sre-jordan: After mitigations (software signer for non-HSM tenants, cached TTL increase, backoff), error rates dropped materially and customer reports stabilized. Still seeing elevated KMS latencies in provider metrics. We're keeping P1 until provider confirms recovery or until we finish a safe rollback to pre-change configs.

eng-ryan: Provider responded: intermittent internal throttling in region us-east-1 affecting KMS control-plane; they are working on a mitigation. They suggested clients use retries with jitter and reduce request rate. We've shared logs and request-ids.

support-anya: Notifying affected customers with a status update: short description, mitigation we applied (software fallback and caching), ETA: monitoring, no ETA from provider yet. Draft prepared for review.

maria-ops: Quick note: avoid mass restarts while provider is degraded — that generates a cold-start surge to KMS. We're blocking all non-urgent deploys and asking teams to hold restarts.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete. New owner: eng-ryan. Please acknowledge to take over incident coordination.

eng-ryan: Acknowledged. I'm owning the incident for the next shift window. Next steps: 1) continue provider engagement until resolved, 2) coordinate customer comms and post-incident RCA, 3) plan durable changes: longer local envelope TTL, improved retry/backoff baked into signer client, and a feature to flag drop-in software signer per tenant safely.

sre-jordan: Adding RCA owners: eng-ryan (mitigation/hotfix), maria-ops (operational runbook updates), support-anya (customer comms). We'll reconvene in incident postmortem channel after provider confirms recovery.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigation in place, monitoring. Keep channel updated with any regression.

eng-ryan: Final note before I escalate: request ids for failed KMS calls: `req-8a6b`, `req-8a6c`, `req-8a6d`. Attached traces uploaded to provider ticket.

support-anya: Customer comms sent to affected customers with links to status page and guidance to use dedicated instances or avoid restarts for now.

maria-ops: Will generate a short postmortem draft template with timeline and action items once provider confirms resolution. Action items so far: longer TTL, default retries+backoff, deploy gating on KMS health metric, and tenant-level fallback controls.

eng-ryan: Logging this thread into the incident tracker and closing the on-call handoff. I'll update when provider gives final status.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: id=INC-2026-03-KMS-1. End of thread for now.
